svg.title: FinOps
svg.desc: FinOps. Cloud cost as a shared responsibility: allocate spend to the teams that cause it, optimise it and track the cost per unit of value. Step 1, A bill nobody owns: June’s AWS bill is $130,000, up from $80,000 in January; 35% has no owner tag and nobody knows why. Step 2, Inform: see and allocate: Tags required, shared costs split by rule, a showback per team: July costs $4.10 per 1,000 orders. Step 3, Optimize: usage, then rate: Usage first (delete, rightsize, schedule), then rate (Savings Plan, Spot): $2.90 per 1,000 orders. Step 4, Operate, and the pitfalls: Budgets, anomaly alerts and a monthly review keep the loop going; the usual pitfalls show in amber.

g.text: June’s AWS bill is $130,000, up from $80,000 in January; 35% has no owner tag and nobody knows why.
Tags required, shared costs split by rule, a showback per team: July costs $4.10 per 1,000 orders.
Usage first (delete, rightsize, schedule), then rate (Savings Plan, Spot): $2.90 per 1,000 orders.
Budgets, anomaly alerts and a monthly review keep the loop going; the usual pitfalls show in amber.

AWS was $130,000 in June. Who spent it?
Our pods sit at 12% CPU. Can’t be us.
The cluster is shared. Can’t split it.

Inform: every dollar has an owner, and the unit cost shows whether growth is efficient
Optimize ranks the options; the owning teams make the changes
Operate: budgets, alerts and a monthly review, every month
pitfall: FinOps done to teams, not with them (“cut 20%” tickets from a central team)
